Added `countWords(str)` to `src/str.js:16` and a test in `test/str.test.js:24`. All 4 tests pass.

"Word" here means whitespace-delimited token — `trim()` then split on `/\s+/`, with an explicit zero guard since splitting `''` yields `['']` and would otherwise report 1 for empty and whitespace-only input.

Worth knowing what that definition does and doesn't cover:
- `'don't'` and `'well-known'` count as one word each; `'a--b'` also counts as one. If you need punctuation to split, this isn't it.
- `\s` in JS regex does match Unicode whitespace including non-breaking space and ideographic space, so those work.
- Scripts without inter-word spaces (Chinese, Japanese, Thai) will count an entire run as one word. `Intl.Segmenter` with `granularity: 'word'` is the real answer there, if it ever matters.

No commits made.
